National Weather Service Burlington VT
244 PM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 241 PM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 241 PM EDT Sunday...

1. Showers and a couple embedded thunderstorms this afternoon 
and evening. 

2. Mostly dry and seasonably cool weather through mid-week. 

3. Periods of unsettled weather continue through the end of the 
week into the weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 241 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A southern stream low will continue to push off to the 
northeast and eastern Vermont will become completely dry by mid-
afternoon. As the center passes to the east, it will help decrease 
the southerly winds and warm air advection. A prefrontal trough will 
move into northern New York from Ontario this afternoon and evening, 
causing a broken line of showers and storms to develop. These will 
be slow moving and should mostly be confined to northern New York 
until 7-8 PM. These will weaken as they push east. Another round of 
showers will move through overnight from northwest to southeast 
associated with the cold front, though low instability should keep 
them weak. A brief strong to severe storm is possible this afternoon 
in the St. Lawrence Valley where instability is the highest. Dew 
points have reached around 70 there and some breaks of sun have 
caused temperatures to rise into the upper 70s. The cloudy marine 
modified airmass farther southeast will cause storms to quickly 
weaken as they try to push east.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Relatively zonal flow will develop heading into mid-
week, though the northern stream energy should mostly stay to the 
north and the southern stream energy should mostly stay to the 
south. The one exception is Tuesday night into Wednesday morning 
where a few showers are possible in northern areas as a dying cold 
front moves into the region. Otherwise, surface high pressure will 
generally remain in control. Efficient radiational cooling will 
cause temperatures to drop into the 30s and 40s on Monday night, 
with patchy frost expected in the coldest hollows of the Adirondacks 
and Northeast Kingdom. Overall, during this stretch, highs will 
generally be in the 60s and 70s with low humidity.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Upper level flow will remain high zonal and unblocked 
next week supporting a series of fast-moving waves moving through 
every 2-3 days. The result will be for continued periods of showers 
with highs around to slightly below seasonal averages and overnight 
lows remaining slightly above averages. Model consensus favors 
trough passage Thursday into Friday, brief high pressure Saturday, 
and another wave potentially late in the weekend into early the 
following week. With wave amplitude remaining shallow, significant 
impacts are unlikely, but some moderate to localized heavier 
precipitation will be possible with the Thursday wave since PWATs 
climb above 1.25". A few rumbles of thunder could occur along the 
front, especially towards southern Vermont. High temperatures are 
favored to remain in the upper 60s to mid 70s with lows generally in 
the mid 40s to mid 50s.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 18Z Monday...Rain and thunderstorms are tracking out of
Vermont and northern New York with most locations becoming partially
clear to clear after 07Z. With ample low level moisture and clearing
skies, fog and stratus will become increasingly likely. IFR
conditions will be most likely at SLK/MPV/EFK, but there is a 10-25%
chance for CIGs to form below 1000ft for most terminals; note the
6sm due to BR and sct002- 004 in the TAFs for BTV/PBG/MSS. MVFR
conditions are more likely at RUT by 08Z as BKN033 sags lower with
decreasing winds aloft. After 12-15Z, conditions improve to VFR with
some northwesterly breezes. Gusts will be 10-20kts. More IFR/MVFR
conditions are expected after 00Z tonight but more of a question of
when it will set up for each terminal in the 02-08Z time frame.

Outlook...

Monday Night: VFR. Patchy BR.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Wednesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 325 AM EDT Sunday...

The Lake Wind Advisory should end this evening. Winds will
continue to decrease this afternoon and they are expected to
drop into the 10-20 KT range for the overnight. Winds will
switch from southerly to west/northwest overnight. Waves will
gradually decrease from 1-3 feet to around 1 foot tonight,
dropping as the wind decreases and the direction becomes more
westerly. 

&&
